source_briefs.title: The Carnac Regio — GM Brief
source_briefs.scope: Five nested Magic-aligned levels beneath the drowned end of the Carnac alignments. Discovered by Dagmar, Spring 1224. Playable 1224–1226.

campaign_clock.detail: Jupiter and Saturn close to 2.1 arcminutes in Aquarius — an evening-sky event, the closest observable great conjunction between 1226 and 2020. It does not unlock a chamber; it makes the level-5 crossing survivable for one night. Hang the lock on the PATH, not the aura: Magic auras do not fluctuate cyclically.
campaign_clock.runway: Fall 1224 → March 1226 — roughly six playable seasons.
campaign_clock.player_facing: Dagmar's established method is premonitions plus astrology, so the date is his to discover in character. Aldebaran (a Behenian fixed star) is the anchor the conjunction points at; the Hyades are the classical rainy stars, which matches the covenant's maritime regio grammar.
campaign_clock.optional: Halley's Comet passed in 1222 — usable in retrospect as what woke the lower levels and produced the 1224 mirror-flash.

scenes.title: Éogan and the capricorn
scenes.hook: On the voyage home from Ireland a Magic-realm capricorn (sea-goat) singles Éogan out and paces his ship — offered as his first familiar prospect. The work is courting it and the binding lab-work, not an instant bond.
scenes.detail:
ADVANCED (Spring 1224): Éogan spotted the capricorn at a river-mouth near Drogheda (it favours salt-meets-fresh water), took a water sample and cast a relocation spell. Courtship and binding are still ahead. Developed: the draw is independent of the 'small fae drawn to Éogan/Stijntje' affinity; its signature specialty is CROSSING THRESHOLDS INTO REGIONES (mythic grounding in Enki's Goat-Fish and Macrobius's Gate of the Gods). Corpus build/bind references and a suggested Might ~12–16 Magic build are recorded. What it wants in exchange remains open.

CARNAC LINK: per the site brief's backstory cascade, the fae were driven WEST into Atlantic and Irish waters c. 225 AD. Éogan's fae attendants (t068) and a Magic capricorn offering itself at an Irish river-mouth are both downstream of the same displacement — a player character is standing in the far end of the Carnac backstory without knowing it.

scenes.title: Confluensis turns the screws — the Grand Tribunal complaint
scenes.hook: The home-front spine for the 22nd: after the public 13th-place "Siege of Shame" at the 1223 Tribunal and Bertrand's cold renege of the book-storage deal, Confluensis moves from soured silence to active reprisal — assembling a complaint against Sjórseiðr while the covenant's magi are scattered north (Dagmar/Valdemar) and south (Wilhelm).
scenes.detail: The documented direction (c022): someone from Confluensis is preparing to bring Rán's open faerie association — and the covenant's OTHER exposed edges — before the Grand Tribunal as a bundled quaesitorial complaint. Live edges it could gather: Valdemar parading the sea-fae Rán at the feast (c022), the unspendable five bags of stolen Roman dragon-gold and its provenance (c026), Mímormr loosed toward the North Sea by Dagmar's errand (t072), and — most dangerous — Wilhelm's ungifted folk-magic teaching with its madness/death toll (t019, t020, q028). Oleron, a Liege that favours Sjórseiðr for beating the other lieges, is the natural counter-ally (t074). What FORM the screw-turning takes first — a formal charge, a whispering campaign, vassal-poaching, or economic pressure through the soured Bertrand arrangement — is the live beat. GM prep 2026-08-09 (t078). Planned opening gambit (t078, 2026-08-15): a FORGED Order-of-Odin letter, manufactured to implicate Valdemar and entered as evidence — details TBD.

scenes.title: The Diedne Garden — a druidic circle on the Channel coast, and the road to initiation
scenes.thread: Vis sources / the Diedne Garden / Valdemar's lineage
scenes.hook: Valdemar has taken on the covenant's newly-won Diedne Garden — a Herbam vis source (3 pawns/yr) on the SOUTH COAST OF THE ENGLISH CHANNEL, not on the Isle of Man. It is an old druidic circle: the ruin of KERGUNTUIL, a Diedne covenant on the Brittany Rose Coast. He can spend the season there harvesting, or he can spend it beginning to initiate himself into the Diedne mystery.
scenes.detail:
═══ PLAYED — Spring 1224, the first visit (session 2026-10-03; arrival per owner 2026-10-04) ═══

ARRIVAL: they had road directions from Flanders, but came by sea and upriver, then explored on foot. They nearly missed it: overgrown, the stones broken and buried.

PARTY: Valdemar, Ka'wa'ill, Garrat Coffin, Leofwin, Oliver, and Eric the minstrel.

THE RITES: Valdemar followed his own memory of the rite over Pliny wherever they differed. One House Diedne Lore roll per herb:
• Mistletoe — exploding success, 3 pawns.
• Selago — failed: viable herbs, no vis.
• Samolus (next morning) — succeeded after 2 Confidence spent: 2 pawns.
TOTAL 5 Herbam — an unusually strong yield (owner); the source is listed at 3/yr. Covenant ledger updated (1224 and current: 3 → 5).

THE DISCOVERY: it came on the FAILED selago roll, not a botch; the botch trigger was set aside in play (owner, 2026-10-04). Ka'wa'ill and Garrat, digging, found a human thigh bone and a skull: no marker, clothing, weapons or grave goods, only broken stones. Eric (Magic Lore, drawn to the lurid stories) pieced the stones: possibly an altar ~3 ft wide, 8–9 ft long, a couple of ft thick. Valdemar ordered no exhumation: the bones were reburied, the stones set in order, the altar left upside down (stable).

NOT DONE (owner): nobody sensed the site and no initiation step was attempted. The taint is undetected and THE NAMING untouched.

WOLVES: lingering since the first day; they attacked at dusk. Leofwin killed one; Ka'wa'ill botched (trident set down; −3 dry). The rest fled before Valdemar's lightning-sheathed blade (a rune of Thor) and his order in Norse to go back to 'their master's kennel' (bluster, or a real master? unruled). The pelt was taken.

AFTERMATH: a couple of days replanting herbs and seeds; Valdemar reported the garden's deliberate destruction to the covenant. Eric now knows Valdemar is Diedne (t090). The next visit is the 1225 harvest (approved: 3 pawns of Herbam).

CORRECTION OF RECORD: the garden is on the Channel's south coast. Earlier notes placing it inside the Ránargarðr holding on Man were wrong and have been struck from s13.

WHY THE SITING IS BETTER: it sits in the Tribunal's heartland, not on a private island. It was won as a Tribunal prize, so its location is a matter of public record — everyone in Normandy knows who holds it. Every season Valdemar spends there is a season a DIEDNE SITE is being visited, repeatedly, by a magus from the covenant Confluensis is building a case against (s11). Part of the ordeal is simply being seen going.

AND IT COSTS HIM SEASONS: Undrahöll on Man (s13), the garden on the Channel, and the raiding that funds both are three different places. He cannot do all of it. Making him choose between his laboratory and his lineage every year is the engine of this thread.

═══ THE GARDEN (prepped 2026-10-03) ═══
THE SITE: the ruin of KERGUNTUIL (920–1007), a fallen Diedne covenant on the Brittany Rose Coast. Sub Rosa #13 ('Unearthing the Thirteenth House') names four Normandy Diedne covenants: Branugurix (the Mount Dol seal) and Caput Capra (the Loire ruins) are already Tribunal catalogue sites, Baiocassium lay in the forest near Bayeux, and Kerguntuil is the only one on the Channel coast.

THE THREE HERBS (tentative): the three plants Pliny's Natural History says the Druids gathered by rite, one pawn of Herbam each.
Mistletoe (NH 16.95): cut from an oak on the sixth day of the moon with a golden sickle, by a gatherer in white, caught in a white cloak. Pliny notes it is rarely found on the oak. (Bostock & Riley's 1855 translation says 'fifth'; the Latin is sexta luna.)
Selago (NH 24.62): gathered without iron, the right hand passed through the left sleeve 'as though the gatherer were in the act of committing a theft'; white clothing, bare and washed feet, an offering of bread and wine first; carried in a new napkin.
Samolus (NH 24.63): grows in damp ground; gathered fasting, with the left hand, without looking back; laid down only in the cattle's drinking troughs.
The modern identity of selago and samolus is uncertain (the translators' notes offer fir club-moss; brookweed, pasque-flower or brooklime), which leaves room for 'unusual herbs.'

THE HARVEST: a Tropaeum is by definition a source 'requiring minimal effort to harvest.' Performed correctly, each rite yields its pawn with no roll. Each broken condition adds a botch die; a botch loses THAT herb for the year. Anyone who has read Pliny can attempt the rites, which is why it can be a Tribunal lease at all; House Diedne Lore supplies what Pliny, a Roman outsider, never saw. The trip itself is cheap (core: a distraction under a month has no effect on study); the real seasonal cost is the initiation below.

═══ THE SECRET (GM only — to be played out) ═══
The garden was a site of HUMAN SACRIFICE, and that is part of how it was empowered: the druidic circle and its aura make the place magical; the sacrificed dead give the herbs their vis. Each herb is an offering to one of the three gods the Commenta Bernensia names (cited in Sub Rosa #13):
Samolus — TEUTATES — the drowned (damp ground; laid only in water troughs; never look back).
Mistletoe — ESUS — the hanged (cut down from the oak).
Selago — TARANIS — the burned (prized for its smoke; taken as though committing a theft).
Read with this in mind, every one of Pliny's conditions is a rite of offering. Pliny himself (NH 30.4) records that the Druids held 'to murder a man was to do an act of the greatest devoutness, and to eat his flesh was to secure the highest blessings of health.'

INFERNAL TAINT: the site carries it. Core (Realms, 'Tainted Vis'): Infernal vis twists projects to evil ends and slowly corrupts the magus using it; it at least doubles spellcasting botch dice and forces the experimental results chart for enchanted items; 'magi should be very wary of discoveries made while working with Infernal vis' — which lands squarely on Valdemar's possible Discovery (t085). Sama (Pious; Sense Holiness and Unholiness) can feel it.

THE FIRST DISCOVERY — TRIGGERED BY A BOTCH (in play it came on a failed roll instead — see PLAYED above): when a harvest botches and the herb fails, someone digs to replant it and turns up the first small, deniable sign of a burial (Lindow Man, the bog body killed by blow, garrotte and cut throat with mistletoe pollen in his gut, is ready texture). The full pattern — three burials, three deaths, three herbs — is there only if they keep digging.

WHAT IT TOUCHES: t085 (the garden as Valdemar's Insight source). t084 (Furtum: Tremere lineage, strongly against sacrifice, and his House holds the Diedne records — he could confirm it; HoH: True Lineages makes human sacrifice House Tremere's principal accusation against Diedne). t078 / s11 (a public Tribunal lease that multiple covenants claim; proof of sacrifice there is the old Tremere charge made true, on a site Valdemar harvests every spring).

═══ THE INITIATION ═══
The Diedne are a thousand years dead, so there is no mystagogue. THE SITE IS THE MYSTAGOGUE — the script is kept in the circle, recoverable a rung at a time, and the Ordeals are things the place demands rather than things a person imposes. Use the published HOUSE DIEDNE LORE (Arcane) ability (Sub Rosa #13, 'The Slumbering Legacy'): by its own text it can be learned through self-discovery, and a season spent initiating the Diedne mysteries grants experience in it, which suits a site with no living mystagogue. Each season in the garden is a script attempt.

THE LADDER (four rungs, capstone deliberately years out):
1. THE NAMING — Outer Mystery. He says his lineage aloud inside the ring, which is the first time he has said it to anything. Grants House Diedne Lore 1. Ordeal cost: minor.
2. THE GREEN SEASON — a modest grove-bound working benefit (study or spontaneous bonus within the circle).
3. THE BENDING — a partial capstone, usable years early: reduce an opponent's Penetration by his House Diedne Lore score. Lets him feel it working before he has earned the whole thing.
4. THE UNBROKEN RING — Major Hermetic Virtue. HALVE an opponent's Penetration total against him.

BALANCE NOTE: halving Penetration is very strong — against a Penetration 40 attack that is a flat −20 on top of Parma. Purely defensive, so it does not warp offence, but it will make him near-unhittable by anything short of a Tribunal. Two tunings, pick one:
  (a) BIND IT TO THE RING — it functions only inside a circle he has consecrated, including small ones he can lay in a season or scribe aboard a ship. Thematically exact, self-limiting, and it makes his HOLDINGS the source of his power rather than his person.
  (b) UNCONDITIONAL, PRICE IN THE FLAWS — TMRE convention is one Flaw per script. For a secret Diedne the right Flaws are not personal hardships but LEGIBILITY: his magic begins resisting in a way no catalogued Hermetic Virtue explains. RECOMMENDED — because Confluensis is assembling a bundled complaint (s11), an anomalous resistance is not a rumour but a demonstrable effect a quaesitor can test for, and Valerian is a former Rhine quaesitor sitting at his own dinner table. The capstone virtue becomes the confession.

STILL TO PREP: (1) does disturbing or Christianising a burial cost that herb? (TBD); (2) whether the herbs' vis itself carries the Infernal taint, and if so what that means for the five pawns already harvested in Spring 1224; (3) who contests the lease (the catalogue: 'multiple covenants claim historical rights'); (4) the Spring window for each rite. Valdemar also means to pick up basic Herbam in order to work it.

STANDING NOTE: Valdemar is secretly House Diedne (t078). Stacked with the Christian lie (s14) and the fief, this is the highest-stakes exposure any PC carries.

═══ REFERENCE DETAIL (everything gathered 2026-10-03 — cut as needed) ═══

DECISIONS SO FAR (owner, 2026-10-03)
• The garden is the ruin of KERGUNTUIL. — yes.
• The three herbs are Pliny's three druid plants, harvested by rite. — yes, tentatively.
• A harvest botch loses that herb for the year (not permanently).
• What the planter left behind: the owner's idea — it was a site of human sacrifice, and that is part of how it was empowered; a small discovery reveals it.
• A. Three herbs = three gods = three deaths. — yes.
• B. The site carries Infernal taint. — yes.
• C. The first discovery is triggered by a harvest botch. — yes.
• D. Does disturbing or Christianising a burial cost that herb? — TBD.
• Use the published House Diedne Lore (Arcane) in place of the made-up cult ability. — yes.

THE SOURCE OF THE LEASE (Tribunal catalogue, tribunal_data.json v011)
• Catalogue entry, verbatim: 'Politically contested. An overgrown garden at a ruined Diedne covenant site still produces three unusual herbs each spring. Multiple covenants claim historical rights.' Herbam, 3 pawns/year, category Tropaeum.
• Tropaeum, as the Tribunal reference page defines it: 'Tribunal common property — won by Tourney lease. Vis sources requiring minimal effort to harvest. Distributed among Tribunal members on seven-year leases through the Hermetic Tourney. The holder of a lease has exclusive rights to harvest.'
• So it is a LEASE, not a holding. If it runs from the 1223 Tourney, it comes up again at the 1230 Tourney — the natural moment for the 'multiple covenants' with historical claims to contest it.
• Won in the 1223 prize draft for 3 of the covenant's 31 prize pawns (draft rule: a vis source costs its annual yield).
• Harvest record: Spring 1224 Valdemar took the three herbs (ledger: 3 pawns received; the event is now approved as 'The Diedne Garden'); Spring 1225 Valdemar (approved: 3 pawns); Spring 1226 unassigned (p120).

THE OTHER DIEDNE SITES ALREADY IN THE CATALOGUE
• Ruins of Caput Capra, Loire (v036, Luctatio, Perdo, annual): 'On the anniversary of the youngest Diedne covenant's fall, a fist-sized lump of fused stone and ash appears in the ruin. Always in a different location. Confluensis apprentices visit annually — harvesting in their presence is diplomatically fraught.'
• The Branugurix Seal, Mount Dol (v037, Luctatio, Vim, 1 pawn/yr if successful, high danger): 'The sealed entrance to the Diedne domus magna thins once yearly. Pressing a hand against the hillside and resisting the seal's pushback (Stamina + Magic Theory 12+) draws out Vim vis. Botching risks being pulled inside. House Guernicus actively watches this site.'
• Note who is already watching Diedne sites: Confluensis (Caput Capra) and House Guernicus (Branugurix).

SUB ROSA #13 — THE FOUR NORMANDY DIEDNE COVENANTS ('Unearthing the Thirteenth House')
• Branugurix (791–1012) — Domus Magna of House Diedne, near Mount Dol in Brittany.
• Baiocassium (851–1011) — in the forest near Bayeux. (Unused so far.)
• Kerguntuil (920–1007) — on the Brittany Rose Coast. → our garden: the only one on the Channel coast.
• Caput Capra (981–1005) — on the banks of the Loire near Fleury.
• Same article: Diedne favoured Arts gave +2 bonuses on Animal and Herbam Forms; 'Magi of House Diedne held their ritual sites sacred to their religion.'
• Cult of Belenos article: Diedne covenants usually sat in a magical aura close to a place of religious worship, near places of each of the elements; named for the local tribal areas, with gods native to those tribes 'either actually walking around, or in statue form.'

HOUSE DIEDNE LORE (Arcane) — published text (Sub Rosa #13, 'The Slumbering Legacy')
• The (Organization) Lore of House Diedne: goals, history, legends, structure; lineages and sects; the theory, mystery-cult rites, and secrets of the Diedne's Nature and Beast oriented magics.
• Primarily orally transmitted; 'it can be learned through self-discovery.' A season spent initiating the Diedne mysteries gains experience in it.
• Specialties: initiations, lineages, legends, sites, Clan Mysteries.
• Note: Sub Rosa's articles disagree — 'The Cult of Belenos' calls its version Diedne Cult Lore. We use House Diedne Lore.

PUBLISHED DIEDNE MYSTERY PATHS, FOR COMPARISON WITH OUR LADDER (Sub Rosa #13, 'The Cult of Belenos'; all run on Diedne Cult Lore)
• PATH OF MISTLETOE — 'relished in the magical power of nature, rather than the spirits themselves.' Seed: Animal Ken, usually gaining the Pagan Flaw. Bud: Major Potent Magic (Forests). Flower: Forest Lore.
• PATH OF ROWAN — summons and bargains with powerful nature spirits; blamed for the appearance of infernalism. Seed: Minor Potent Magic (Spirits or Gods), Pious as ordeal. Bud: Second Sight. Flower: the Goetic Art of Summoning (Magic or Faerie). Decay: the Binding Goetic Art, usually suffering the Tainted with Evil Flaw.
• PATH OF TONGUES — power over the dead through the heads of enemies. Seed: Second Sight, usually with the Pagan Flaw. Bud: Major Potent Magic of Heads. Flower: the Hermetic Binding mystery.
• The house also initiated the Diedne Ceremony ability without requiring any path.

PLINY'S NATURAL HISTORY — FULL DETAIL (Bostock & Riley translation, 1855, public domain; checked on Perseus and against the Latin)
• MISTLETOE (16.95, 'Historical Facts Connected with the Mistletoe'): the Druids hold nothing more sacred than mistletoe and the tree that bears it, always the oak (robur); it is rarely found on the oak and is gathered 'with rites replete with religious awe.' Chiefly on the SIXTH day of the moon — the beginning of their months, years and thirty-year ages; they call the moon by a name meaning 'the all-healing.' Sacrifice and a banquet are prepared beneath the trees; two white bulls are brought, horns bound for the first time; a priest in a white robe climbs and cuts the mistletoe with a GOLDEN SICKLE, caught by others in a white cloak; the victims are then immolated with prayers. Belief: taken in drink it gives fecundity to barren animals and is an antidote to all poisons. (The 1855 translation says 'fifth day'; the Latin is 'ante omnia sexta luna' — sixth.)
• SELAGO (24.62): 'similar to savin.' Gathered without iron, the right hand passed through the left sleeve of the tunic 'as though the gatherer were in the act of committing a theft'; clothing white, feet bare and washed clean, a sacrifice of bread and wine made first; carried in a new napkin. The Druids of Gaul say it should be carried as a preservative against accidents of all kinds, and its smoke is extremely good for all maladies of the eyes. (Identity disputed — footnotes offer fir club-moss.)
• SAMOLUS (24.63): named by the Druids; grows in humid localities. Gathered fasting, with the left hand, as a preservative against the maladies of swine and cattle; the gatherer must not look behind him, and it must be laid nowhere but in the troughs from which the cattle drink. (Identity disputed — footnotes offer brookweed/water-pimpernel, pasque-flower, or brooklime.)
• DRUID SACRIFICE (30.4, 'The Druids of the Gallic Provinces'): Tiberius put down the Druids 'and all that tribe of wizards and physicians'; Britain still cultivates the art 'with ceremonials so august.' Rome ended 'those monstrous rites, in accordance with which, to murder a man was to do an act of the greatest devoutness, and to eat his flesh was to secure the highest blessings of health.' — the same book that teaches the harvest rite records the sacrifice (and t085's 'consuming a human').
• Pliny's claimed virtues (fecundity/antidote; warding accidents and eye-smoke; protecting swine and cattle) are ready-made non-vis uses for the herbs if anyone tries them.

HUMAN SACRIFICE — WHAT THE SOURCES SAY
• Core line (HoH: True Lineages, Guernicus chapter): House Tremere's principal accusation against House Diedne was human sacrifice.
• Sub Rosa #13 ('Unearthing'): HoH:TL p.113 has the Tremere's 'deeper reason for their loathing of the Diedne wicker men'; the wicker man (Taranis) burned criminals or prisoners. The 10th-century Commenta Bernensia: victims for TEUTATES were drowned, for ESUS hanged, for TARANIS burned. Hedge Magic RE lists Toranos the thunder god. Sub Rosa's conclusion: 'there is no myth here; House Diedne practised human sacrifice.'
• Sub Rosa #13 ('Cult of Belenos'): among the Celts, sacrifice was relatively rare, kept for great need (long droughts, threats to the whole village); the victims likely the old, the sick or the deformed, sometimes willing. Some Diedne collected enemies' heads and bound spells of protection and necromancy into them on poles; some practised ritual sacrifice of their own members to protect their knowledge into their next reincarnated life.
• Fits our Infernal taint — Sub Rosa's 'Hypothesis One': the Diedne leadership were fooled by False Gods who granted them infernal powers and masked them; 'their spells were unable to detect their own magics were tainted.' The Diedne may never have known the garden was tainted.
• Mechanical precedent for sacrifice → vis (Sub Rosa #13, 'Slumbering Legacy'): Magical Sacrifice (Minor Supernatural) — sacrificing a Magic or Faerie creature in ritual casting destroys it and yields 50% more of its vis, with an extra botch die per pawn so generated.
• Published precedent for a death-fed vis source (Covenants): The Hangman's Oak yields one blood-red Corpus acorn in each year a man is hanged from it.
• Lindow Man (real, 1984, Lindow Moss, Cheshire): bog body killed by a blow to the head, a garrotte and a cut throat ('triple death'), with mistletoe pollen in the gut — texture for the damp corner where the samolus grows.

INFERNAL TAINT — THE RULES IN PLAY
• Core, Realms, 'Tainted Vis': Infernal vis 'tends to twist any project to evil ends, and slowly corrupt a magus's personality as he works with it. At the very least, using Infernally tainted vis adds twice as many botch dice as usual to spellcasting, and requires a roll on the experimental results chart for an enchanted item. Magi should be very wary of discoveries made while working with Infernal vis.'
• If you give the burial spots a small Infernal aura, the Realm Interaction Table applies (Reference Guide): Magic powers −aura in an Infernal aura, and +1 botch die per aura rating in a foreign aura.
• Sama's Sense Holiness and Unholiness (Reference Guide, DE p170): a general area is Ease Factor 9; a person or object 15; it must penetrate Magic Resistance and is granted by the Divine realm.

DESIGN NOTES — HOW PUBLISHED PLANT VIS SOURCES WORK (Covenants, vis-source examples)
• A discrete physical yield tied to a precise moment (The Cursed Tree drops one golden acorn at sundown on the eve of spring).
• A condition that costs future yield if broken (Apples of Hesperides: six golden apples a year, three must be left to rot; each missing apple adds a botch die, and each botch permanently drops the yield by one) — our 'lose that herb for the year' is the gentler version.
• A social price for greed (Lovers' Violets: take up to half and earn only a mild reputation; take all and the town sours).
• A mystery uncovered once collecting is routine (Circle of Destroying Angel Mushrooms: the vis grows where an Unseelie lord's doomed dancer died; locals hide on holy ground the night before the Vernal Equinox).
• A vis source's Art need not match the plant (Mallorn Dandelions are Herbam plants yielding Auram vis).

scenes.title: Level 5 — the road, and the March 1226 lock
scenes.hook: Not a room. The far side. The conjunction of 4–5 March 1226 does not unlock a chamber — it makes the crossing survivable, for one night.
scenes.detail:
UPDATE (owner review 2026-09-19): the party reached Level 4 (Fall 1224) and confirmed the deeper way is sealed until the 4-5 March 1226 conjunction; Llewellyn elected to remain in the regio to be present when it opens, and Dagmar undertook to return by then. This scene is the March 1226 return. RoP:M notes that gateways into the Magic Realm proper are guarded by fierce creatures on the FAR side and typically open inward only; insulae are theorised as Magic regiones above aura 10, and aura 10 already reads in core as a gateway to the realm of its affiliation.

THE INVERSION, stated plainly: the goal is not to reach level 5. It is to be standing in the throne room in March 1226 and prevent the stairs from appearing — while the only people who know the building are convinced the party has come to rob their church.

HANG THE LOCK ON THE PATH, NOT THE AURA. Magic auras do not fluctuate cyclically; the aura stays 10 and only the stairs are conditional. DE's Ease-Factor language covers this explicitly.

LLEWELLYN'S PRIZE (§10). RoP:M gives three unprovable models of the Magic Realm — cosms, the Magic Archipelago (insulae and Ferrymen), and tempora (deeper = older; popular with Criamon, which is Dagmar's house). Orkney was already a COSM reading: room-sized spherical microcosms hanging in liquid sky. Carnac in the archipelago idiom is the same phenomenon under a different theory. Two magi, two models, one regio, incompatible maps — exactly the trap Erobos warned about, and exactly the ammunition Llewellyn needs. The published text says sustained exploration by a group of magi MIGHT make one theory harder to sustain, and that the storyguide then decides the underlying truth. That is a campaign-length prize and it is on the table.

OPTIONAL: A. Vibert Douglas identified five conjunctions across 1226–27. If you want the number five doing extra work — five conjunctions, five levels, each keyed to one, the fifth simply the last to arrive.

scenes.title: London — brokering the dragon's gold
scenes.hook: Tormente handed Dagmar a brokerage errand — sell the Roman 'debris' gold on the dragon's behalf. London, the nearest gold market, is where it has to be converted, and the covenant already has form there.
scenes.detail: UPDATE (owner review 2026-09-19): DEFERRED. Exiting Carnac (Fall 1224), Tormente put the brokerage on hold — 'ask me in a few years' — so the covenant is converting the five bags on its own account for now. Park until the dragon revisits it. STUB for next session. The recovered Roman dragon-gold is now Tormente's, and Dagmar owes it a sale. The problem is the one c026 already mapped: a silver-standard economy with no gold coinage, treasure-trove law, and provenance questions — melt to bullion, use a discreet fence / Jewish moneylender / Lombard banker, or commission worked goods. Foxglove knows the London fence from the earlier run (verified events). Live beats: how much of the coin to convert and how (melt vs sell-as-is), what Dagmar reports back to Tormente, and whether the covenant's own Flanders/Bruges bullion channels are now open since the theft is resolved.

scenes.title: Durenmar — the Great Library, the Roots, and who's in residence
scenes.hook: Spring 1225: Wilhelm goes home to Durenmar, the covenant that trained him, for books, Roots, a stone sled, and his research assistants. The house that made him is run by a faction that despises exactly what his research is, and in three years it hosts the Grand Tribunal where his folk-magic teaching is meant to be put on trial.
scenes.detail:
═══ PLAYED — Spring 1225 (session 2026-10-03) ═══
• Wilhelm found the stone-sled lab text in Durenmar's library and built two sleds himself in his old lab: 2 Terram each, 4 total (owner); Lab Total just scraping 40. His experiment rolled a special/story event (unresolved — q044).
• The Roots: Hilda copied the five the Great Library holds (Intellego, Muto, Herbam, Ignem, Animal) in one season, quickly, so each is Level 6 / Quality 23; they are in the covenant library (owner, 2026-10-04). The other four (Auram, Rego, Aquam, Vim) would come by Redcap.
• Sent thesis 1.0 with a spellbook round his old circle. Reception: grudging respect.
• Overheard the Grand Tribunal complaint against Valdemar and copied the paperwork (t078; p139).
• Visited Dietrich at Cologne (ideas for scaling up teaching); flew his family to Man at the start of Winter 1225-26 (p140).
The material below stays as reference for later Durenmar visits and the Grand Tribunal there in 1228.

WHY THIS SCENE BITES: Durenmar's leadership is purist (enhance and purify Hermetic theory; no 'inferior' magics; intolerant of hedge wizardry), and Wilhelm's whole project is integrating folk magic for the ungifted. His natural allies here are the House's tolerated outsiders. Sources in brackets: GotF = Guardians of the Forests: The Rhine Tribunal (Ars Magica Open License text); HoH:TL = Houses of Hermes: True Lineages; RoP:M = Realms of Power: Magic.

THE PLACE
• Domus magna of House Bonisagus and the oldest covenant: the Founders swore the Code here in 767, on the ruins of a Roman (Mercurian) temple. A valley floor ~15 miles into the northern Black Forest; Hirsau monastery, 15 miles north, rumours a 'hidden city of sorcerers.' [GotF; HoH:TL; core]
• Arrival: a guard post at the valley foot hides a 3-mile track; visitors reach a mill with a small guard tower, where a bell is rung for an arriving magus. [GotF]
• Visitors are formally welcomed at Notatus's standing stone (site of the first Aegis of the Hearth) and given a token so the Aegis does not penalise their casting. [GotF]
• Magic aura 7, under a very high-magnitude Aegis; no walls at all — seclusion and magic instead. [GotF; RoP:M]
• Three towers: Bonisagus (the Great Library, wrapped by an ancient vine said to be Merinita's gift, whose golden-green sap is Intellego vis); Notatus (the Bonisagus sancta; Murion holds the top two floors); Trianoma (crooked, top two floors gone; Trianomae, non-Bonisagus residents, and the Mercer House in its basements). [GotF; HoH:TL]
• The Forum of Hermes holds the Rhine Tribunal and the Grand Tribunals; its chamber seats 120. [GotF; HoH:TL]
• Verditius' Forge, half-underground, is the Artificer's home. Philippus's Watchtower stands on the cliff in a ring of blasted ground (his basilisk withers plants). Seneca's Folly, a collapsed wooden tower, is the cautionary tale told to apprentices. [GotF]
• An 'Autumn covenant verging on Winter': inward-looking, infrastructure crumbling, short of vis, still carrying the 1151 conviction for plundering the Black Forest's faerie sites. Fengheld has quietly overtaken it in the Tribunal. [GotF]
• Covenfolk are old, odd, warped by the aura (everyone has a Warping Flaw), keep relics of an old pagan nature cult, and have no church. The autocrat Sula (90+) arranges guests and knows exactly who they are. [GotF]

THE GREAT LIBRARY
• The largest collection of Hermetic books in existence; the only library that tries to own everything. Around a dozen magi are studying in it in any season. [GotF; Covenants]
• House rule: 'those who study from the Great Library must also contribute.' Each accepted contribution buys two seasons of study; a season of copying buys one (apprentice work); a quiet 'donation' of vis is accepted in practice. House Bonisagus and members are exempt — so Wilhelm studies free and takes priority over equal-rank outsiders. [GotF]
• For a Bonisagus, depositing his work here counts as fulfilling the Oath to share it: enquirers can simply be referred to the library. This is where Wilhelm's Insight Lab Texts and tractatus would go (t087, q039). [GotF; HoH:TL]
• Andrus, the librarian, decides which contributions are accepted and whether visitors may copy or remove anything. Two magi wanting one tome in a season: rank decides, then Bonisagus/members, then certamen. [GotF]
• Texts on exotic theory and hedge traditions are pulled from the shelves into the librarian's sanctum (floors 6–7), open only to House elders — the very material Wilhelm needs. [GotF]
• Floors: 1st scriptorium, forgotten lab notes, and the complete Rhine and Grand Tribunal records plus the House folios; 2nd hundreds of Lab Texts; 3rd Ability and Art books (three copies of Principia Magica; at least one outstanding summa per Art); 4th–5th four visitor labs; basement behind an enchanted iron trapdoor holds the originals, the vis stores, and Founders' relics. [GotF]
• Lookup rules [GotF]: a standard spell's Lab Text is there on a stress die vs EF 3; a specific Art summa on a simple die + 10 (+3 for Bonisagus, masters or members) vs its level. Durenmar Lore can add to the Quality roll.
• Labs for hire: guest-quarter labs at 2 pawns a season; the Tower of Notatus basement labs for masters and archmagi at 5 pawns a season. [GotF]
• Set dressing: the Forest of Shining Stone, Bonisagus's The Art of Magic etched into 36 six-foot crystals; the largest codex, of Mercurian rituals, with a life-size Wizard's Communion diagram to stand on; reading rooms where requests slide down a wax-slate chute so visitors never meet a librarian's eye. [Covenants]
• The Tabula Geographica Magica, House Bonisagus's gazetteer of magical sites and regiones, is kept here and shared reluctantly — a place Kerguntuil or the Carnac stack might be recorded. [HoH:TL]

WHO'S IN RESIDENCE (ten Bonisagus magi, five from other Houses) [GotF]
• MURION, Prima of House Bonisagus (98, archmage). Haughty, judgmental; wants Durenmar and the Rhine restored to dominance. Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal and leader of the Oak Gild. Brilliant in Rego and Imaginem; a white feather cloak of illusions; her raven Kolkrabus spies on rivals in breach of the Code. Backs the Ash Gild's plan to invade the Norse lands.
• ANDRUS (61, master). Murion's first filius, the librarian and a Colens Arcanorum; always present, overworked, commanding stare. Controls library access — 'most unwise to annoy him.' Seen as Murion's puppet; rumoured to want archmagehood.
• TANDALINE (78, master of Muto and Auram). Turns herself to vapour to study Auram. Trianomae, Murion's closest confidante and a Tenens Occultorum; writes to Bonisagi everywhere and will cause great trouble for anyone reported to be abusing a Bonisagus magus. LEVER: Scarem Montem took a Bonisagus's thesis and is using it on Montverte's villeins (t086).
• CAECILIUS (~160, archmage). The greatest living Intellego magus and the Rhine's senior Quaesitor — reluctant, Twilight-prone, but a brilliant investigator with a spotless record. Silver-coated wolf familiar.
• OCCULTES (72, master). Colourful and friendly; manuscripts, enchanted texts and quills, a small golem. Leader of the Linden Gild and figurehead of the outward-looking faction that wants hedge wizardry folded into Hermetic magic; a minority would rather he were Primus. Former librarian, sacked by the previous Primus — and he secretly copied the restricted hedge texts into his own sanctum and quietly lends them to allies. WILHELM'S NATURAL PATRON.
• RICARDUS CAESPUUS (56, master). A recluse in a glass-walled Herbam laboratory full of exotic plants, from which he cultivates several kinds of vis. Earnest, friendly, and incomprehensible. Murion's faction calls him little better than a hedge wizard; he is kept for his vis yields. An ally for Wilhelm, and the man to ask about the Diedne Garden's herbs.
• PETRUS VIRILIS (32, journeyman). Shy and mediocre; his semen is Vim vis, and on Murion's orders he has fathered five Gifted children. Secretly plans a longevity ritual that would likely end it — Murion would be furious.
• WINFRIDA of Guernicus (27, journeyman Quaesitor). Timid, wishes she were a researcher; Murion is grooming her.
• PHILIPPUS NIGER of Flambeau (125, archmage), Protector of Durenmar and leader of the Ash Gild, which wants to strike the Norse wizards beyond the Baltic. His life's work is defending the Order against non-Hermetic wizards: Code of Hermes (hedge wizards), Magic Lore (Norse wizards), a power to smell magic on those who carry it, and a spell built to shatter rune-magic. Basilisk familiar, Sordus. DANGER for Valdemar; hostile to Wilhelm's ungifted folk magic.
• GUDRUN TIGURINA of Verditius, the Artificer, in Verditius' Forge. The obvious seller of Wilhelm's stone sled (q033: 6 pawns Terram).
• XAVIER of Mercere, the Rhine's only Gifted Mercere and its archivist; the Mercer House here runs a Mercere Portal to Harco. The Redcap route for the Roots.
• Plus up to six guest peregrinatores (one per gild at least) on a long waiting list, and three further Bonisagus magi the book leaves unnamed.

WHAT WILHELM CAME FOR (p104)
• Raise Artes Liberales and Philosophiae; acquire books, including one or more Roots (below); buy a stone sled (6 pawns Terram, ruling q033); reconnect with his research assistants Carl & Isaac.
• He is coming home: Durenmar trained him. His graduation project was the Ever-Full Grain Dish, which he had in casual use for weeks before thinking to mention it to his hosts. A Scarem Montem magus called his grasp of Tribunal law 'surprisingly thorough for a magus of Durenmar.' Furtum trained here too.

ROOTS — WHAT THE RULES SAY AND WHAT WE RULED
• Covenants p.93, 'Standard Texts', verbatim: 'For nine of the Arts, there is a basic text that, over time, has come to be accepted as the preferred primer for a magus seeking the competence necessary to train an apprentice. These texts, called the Roots of the Arts, are widely and cheaply available. A Redcap can arrange the delivery of any of these texts, for a very small consideration.'
• ONLY NINE ARTS HAVE A ROOT (Covenants p.93). OWNER RULING 2026-10-04: the nine are AURAM, INTELLEGO, HERBAM, REGO, ANIMAL, IGNEM, AQUAM, VIM and MUTO. Creo, Perdo, Corpus, Imaginem, Mentem and Terram have none. The book gives no titles; the titles below are the placeholders invented on 2026-09-30.
• Same passage: two Roots have been superseded, 'each time by a magus of renown and intelligence.' The finest summae, the BRANCHES of the Arts (eight Arts), are by the Order's custom given as gifts rather than sold, and younger covenants surreptitiously offer payments and services for one.
• Same passage: 'Certain magi consider the root and branch symbolism employed in the advertising of standard texts to be a vestigial druidical practice. They refer instead to the Foundations and Pillars of the Arts.' — a druid echo to use alongside the Diedne Garden.
• Kevin's reading (player notes, 2026-09-19): no numbers are given, but by their description the Roots must be at least L5/Q15; the 'very small consideration' is the troupe's to set.
• RULING q034 (owner, 2026-09-20): the covenant's standard Roots are L6 / Q24 summae, Redcap-deliverable for a small consideration. L6/Q24 sits above the L5/Q15 floor and leaves cushion for quick apprentice copies (Juvenilia, about −3 quality, stay readable). Exceptional Roots (L7/Q28, dragonskin-bound) are effectively unobtainable in play. A specific Root enters the library only when actually acquired.
• Why Q24 is RAW-consistent (Covenants sidebar): most traded summae have qualities 'somewhere between (31 – level) and (28 – level)' — Q22–25 at level 6. Juvenilia lose quality from apprentices' 'typical lack of a Profession: Scribe score.'
• STILL OPEN: the price of the 'very small consideration' (never set); which Roots Wilhelm leaves with (q035). Once played, add each to the library at L6/Q24 (covenant_ledger.json library) and log the cost.

ACQUIRING ROOTS AT DURENMAR
• Roots are 'widely and cheaply available', so the easy route is the Mercer House: Xavier of Mercere arranges Redcap delivery (the Mercere Portal runs to Harco).
• Durenmar's own library is not a shop: visitors may not take books out or copy them without the librarian's (Andrus's) explicit permission; Durenmar occasionally trades tomes like-for-like; its finest works are never sold, only given with ceremony, and copying them is limited to one magus at a time chosen by the Primus's representative. [GotF; Covenants]
• Membership question: ships.json lists Wilhelm's affiliation as Rhine Tribunal (Durenmar), and in Spring 1224 he was invited to formalize membership in Sjórseiðr. If he still counts as a member of Durenmar, he may take Lab Texts to his own lab (members are still expected to study other books inside the library). Either way, as a Bonisagus he studies free and takes priority. [GotF]
• Copy requests can be sent by Redcap with vis to cover the scribing — but the covenant is 'notoriously slow' at them. [GotF]
• Copying one himself (Reference Guide, Writing Books): Copying Carefully = 1 tractatus a season, or 6 + Profession (Scribe) points toward a summa; an Art summa needs points equal to its level (core), so an L6 Root is one careful season. Copying Quickly is three times as fast, with the copy's quality 1 lower.
• Study value (Reference Guide, Advancement Tables): an Art at 6 needs 21 xp, so one season with a Q24 Root takes an untrained Art straight to the summa's cap of 6 (standard ArM5: a summa can't raise an Art past its level). For Wilhelm that matters only for his Arts at 5 or below.

The nine Roots (all L6 / Q24; placeholder titles):
• At Durenmar in 1225 (owner): Intellego — On the Discernment of Truths; Muto — Proteus Bound; Herbam — The Green Mantle; Ignem — First Sparks; Animal — Of Beasts and Their Natures.
• Not at Durenmar: Auram — The Root of Wind and Tempest; Rego — The Ordered Hand; Aquam — The Courses of Water; Vim — The Raw Stuff of Magic.
NOTE: a Root (Level 6) only advances an Art below 6. Wilhelm's Rego and Vim are far above it; all five Durenmar Roots cover Arts where he is 2 or lower, and so do Auram and Aquam. A specific Root enters the library only when actually acquired (q034). How the five could be had is set out in q035.

THREADS TO PULL
• THE GRAND TRIBUNAL, SUMMER 1228, IS HELD HERE (p109). Confluensis plans its bundled complaint (including Wilhelm's ungifted teaching and its death toll, q028) and the Scarem Montem secession question is expected. Whoever Wilhelm wins or loses at Durenmar in 1225 is in the room in 1228.
• Occultes vs Murion is the House's live schism; Wilhelm's research is exactly the kind of work that makes him a pawn or a prize in it.
• Valdemar: the Prima backs a Norse war and the Protector built a spell against rune-magic; Confluensis already suspects him of being an Order of Odin initiate (t078).
• The Fane of the Founders: every seven years, during the Rhine Tribunal, twelve magi (one per House) secretly renew the Founders' vows in a glade near Durenmar; since the Schism War a lineage of Ex Miscellanea has taken Diedne's place. [GotF]

GM SECRETS
• The Black Fir, whose cones the magi greedily harvest as Perdo vis, is the King of the Black Mountain's slow revenge: it sprang up at the Aegis's edge, the magi moved the Aegis to take it inside, and for over a century it has crept about six inches a year toward the Great Library. Nobody remembers it moving. [GotF]
• Trianoma's ghost: HoH:TL's story seed has Trianoma insist on being murdered at the 832 Grand Tribunal to permanently raise the valley's aura; her apprentice did it, her ghost is bound in her tower, and its top two stories were destroyed trying to remove her. GotF calls it a forgotten accident. It mirrors the Diedne Garden secret: the Order's birthplace was empowered by a ritual death too.
• Durenmar secretly holds a few magestones — portable aura tethers attributed to Verditius. [RoP:M]

scenes.title: Wilhelm's research — clarifying Winter 1223-24 → Winter 1224-25
scenes.hook: Wilhelm's folk-magic research exists on record only as unreviewed proposed events across three winters and a spring. Clarify what actually landed each season — Insights, written integrations, breakthrough points — and promote it before any of it can be logged.
scenes.detail:
THE GAP: the research is captured only as proposed events, unreviewed. Nothing is logged in the XP tracker or the library until the mechanical outcome of each season is pinned down and the entries are promoted.

THE THREE SEASONS:
Winter 1223-24 (p049) — wintering at Carrick, Wilhelm cracks the formulaic-ritual integration (drop the divide-by-two; add Artes Liberales + Philosophiae), judging it "really easy — someone just needed to point it out," and sends the assistants out to gather. The real labor is formalizing the Artes Liberales / Philosophiae contribution.
Spring 1224 (p066) — newly aboard the Hound of Cassel, he begins writing two integrations: one to add Artes Liberales, one to let spells be cast "virtually," aiming to finish them as a Factus by year's end.
Winter 1224-25 (p075) — wintering at the Isle of Man, he gets the integrations up and running and sets Carl & Isaac back to gathering.

TO CLARIFY (per the q039 cheat sheet): for each season, which step of the Insight → Integration loop actually happened — an Insight gained (Int + Magic Theory vs EF 18), an effect created, or breakthrough points banked — and against which secret target (Minor 30 / Major 45 / Hermetic 60). Decide what, if anything, is a finished, shareable Insight Lab Text or tractatus by now, and log the XP and any library additions. Fold in the confirmed madness/death cost (q028) as the system's price.

FORWARD: Spring 1225 (p104) has Wilhelm at Durenmar raising Artes Liberales + Philosophiae and sourcing Roots (q035) — the research continues there, and on publication it may earn him a Bonisagus reputation (t087).

UPDATE (2026-10-03 session): Kevin says the experimentation rolls for all three seasons are in Wilhelm's diary entries and he will message which ones. From memory: no Twilight, nothing interesting discovered, 'we just made the spell.' Durenmar (Spring 1225) is now played: see p104 and q044.

UPDATE (2026-10-04): the player supplied the seasons. Winter 1223-24: Ward of the Secure Grainery integrated (p049). Spring 1224: adventuring (tracker). Summer 1224: Blessing of the Fine Harvest integrated (p066). Fall 1224: new summa written (p143). Winter 1224-25: on Man, activity still to choose (q050). XP is recorded; spell levels, breakthrough points, the summa's level and the extra Folk Magic Theory are q045–q049.

scenes.title: Valdemar's defence — the Code, Valerian, and the complaint
scenes.hook: Wilhelm has brought home a copy of the complaint being filed for the 1228 Grand Tribunal: Valdemar is accused of being Order of Odin and of molesting the fae. 1226 opens with Valdemar wanting to study the Code with Valerian, and with the covenant asking who can defend him.
scenes.detail:
WHAT THE TABLE HAS (all played, 2026-10-03):
• THE CHARGES as Wilhelm overheard them at Durenmar: a Normandy covenant (unnamed at the table) accuses a magus of being a member of the Order of Odin, in opposition to the Order and its Oaths, and of molestation of the fae at a Tribunal. A Durenmar colleague called it largely accusatory, 'basically a placeholder', with supplements promised. Wilhelm copied the formal paperwork.
• THE ORDER OF ODIN, as generally understood (GM narration): a catch-all, not a structure; some groups have come into the Order (ex Miscellanea, or trained under other magi) and lost their old traditions; stubborn holdouts keep bespoke amalgams like Valdemar's. Treated as a milder, far-off version of the Diedne: a nuisance, not an existential threat — yet. Wilhelm's reading: a geographical label more than an organisation, and a historical bogeyman.
• VALDEMAR'S LINE: you accuse me of belonging to an order that doesn't exist; and the fae in question is my wife.
• THE REAL THREAT (Wilhelm): a pretext to make Valdemar show or write up his rune magic for integration, leaving him too useful to the Order to be let go.

WHO CAN DEFEND HIM (scores from magi.json):
• Valerian de Castellane — Code of Hermes 3 (Political Intrigue), Civil & Canon Law 6, Common Law 4. NOT in good standing: he knows members of the Rhine Tribunal have suborned the bishopric of Liège, was imprisoned for it until the covenant rescued him, and the only venue for that accusation is the Grand Tribunal (nobody has had the stomach for it). Best as a preparer, not necessarily the public advocate.
• Wilhelm Stienauer — Code of Hermes 2 (Tribunal Procedures).
• Valdemar himself — Code of Hermes 1 (Exceptions & Loopholes); he declared study of the Code with Valerian, then Certamen (p105).

PRESSURE POINTS (GM): Eric now knows Valdemar is Diedne (t090), and Confluensis does not (t078 intel note). The garden is a public lease, and it now has bones and an altar under it (s12). Rán's open fae marriage is the 'molestation' charge's whole substance (c022).

ALSO OPENING 1226: the Great Conjunction (4–5 March 1226) and the Carnac level-5 lock — who attends (s18, p110).

STILL TO PREP: the supplements Confluensis promised (what evidence, and when it is filed); whether Valerian will stand up publicly; what the Order of Odin charge needs to prove under the Code.
